*GitHub profile statistics for any user, as one summary table.*

> **Never compute a stat by hand — every number comes from one deterministic script.**

## Why install this

Asking a model "how many stars does this user have" produces a plausible number.
Every metric here comes from a single shell script running `gh` and `jq`, so the
arithmetic is reproducible and auditable, and the model's job is to decide what
to show rather than what the number is.

It is a conversational re-make of the standalone
[`github-stats-cli`](https://github.com/natejswenson/github-stats-cli) app, with
the same metric definitions, checked against it by a numeric-parity eval.

## What you get

| Path | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `skills/github-stats/SKILL.md` | What Claude reads — the lean core flow. |
| `skills/github-stats/scripts/gh-stats.sh` | The deterministic core: all the `gh` + `jq` arithmetic. |
| `skills/github-stats/reference/commands.md` | The full command catalog, including the confirmation-gated repo-creation flow. |
| `skills/github-stats/tests/` | Network-free unit tests plus a gated live smoke test. |
| `skills/github-stats/eval/` | Numeric parity against the original CLI. |

## Quick start

```bash
scripts/gh-stats.sh overview octocat          # summary table
scripts/gh-stats.sh overview octocat --json   # raw numbers
scripts/gh-stats.sh stars   torvalds          # one metric
scripts/gh-stats.sh repos   octocat           # repo browser
scripts/gh-stats.sh repo    octocat Spoon-Knife
```

Subcommands: `overview`, `commits`, `followers`, `stars`, `prs`, `issues`,
`repos`, `repo`. Read-only commands accept a trailing `--json`.

Install from the [claude-skills marketplace](https://github.com/natejswenson/claude-skills),
or just ask.

## Triggers

- "github stats"
- "github-stats"
- "how many stars/followers/commits does &lt;user&gt; have"
- A GitHub profile summary, or repo stats for an account.
- Creating a repository while looking at stats — which is confirmation-gated and
  never automatic.

## Requirements

- [`gh`](https://cli.github.com/), authenticated (`gh auth login`). The skill
  uses your existing auth; there is no separate token to manage.
- [`jq`](https://jqlang.github.io/jq/) for JSON aggregation.

## Development

```bash
cd skills/github-stats/skills/github-stats
shellcheck scripts/gh-stats.sh   # lint the core
pytest tests/ -v                 # network-free unit tests
python eval/run_eval.py          # parity vs the original CLI (needs gh auth + that repo)
```

Python skill. `ci / github-stats` runs the network-free tests plus the house
lints on every pull request; the parity eval is manual, because it needs
credentials and a second checkout.
